newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen lacking energy for break above 126.50.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen lacking energy for break above 126.50.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to be range-bound, taking a breather from recent rallies on Friday.
The September is likely to be capped at around 126.50, as investors are keen to sell cash bonds at that level, a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
"Yesterday, investors were eager to sell long-term cash bonds at around 126.50, which I think will become near-term resistance," the trader said.
On the downside, the September may seek to fill a gap between 126.28 and 126.32, traders said.

"JGBs might try and fill a gap which exists near 126.28, where it is likely to be supported. But even if it breaks below that level, it is hard to imagine a dip below 126.00 during the day," the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.

JGBs fell on LIFFE overnight due to a comment by Keidanren chairman Shoichiro Toyoda that the Japanese economy appears to be improving and it may be time to raise the official discount rate, traders said.
But this is not the first time the Keidanren chief has made comments calling for a rise in interest rates, so the overall impact on the market is likely to be limited, they said.
Even if the September stalls on Friday as expected, the basic trend for JGBs is up, traders said.

"Traders are becoming very conscious of the record-high of 127.34 for any benchmark futures contract, and the all-time low of 2.075 percent for the key JGB yield," a trader for another trust bank's securities unit said.
